topic: How air-source heat pumps keep a house warm in winter

facts.fact: refrigerant carries heat from outside air
the compressor raises the refrigerant temperature
COP around 3: about three units of heat per unit of electricity
efficiency drops as it gets colder, cold-climate models work well below freezing
defrost cycle clears ice from the outdoor coil

search_results.title: Heat pump basics: moving heat instead of making it
search_results.snippet: A heat pump does not burn fuel to make heat. It moves heat that already exists in the outside air into the house, using a refrigerant that boils at very low temperatures, so even cold outdoor air can warm it up.

search_results.title: The refrigeration cycle, step by step
search_results.snippet: The refrigerant absorbs heat in the outdoor coil and turns to vapour. A compressor squeezes that vapour, which raises its temperature to well above room temperature. Indoors it condenses and releases the heat, then passes an expansion valve and the loop repeats.

search_results.title: What COP means for your energy bill
search_results.snippet: Efficiency is measured as the coefficient of performance (COP): heat delivered divided by electricity used. A typical air-source unit has a COP of about 3 in mild winter weather, so one kilowatt-hour of electricity delivers roughly three kilowatt-hours of heat.

search_results.title: Do heat pumps work in freezing weather?
search_results.snippet: COP falls as the outdoor temperature drops because there is less heat to collect. Modern cold-climate models still heat effectively at -15°C, and some are rated down to -25°C, though a backup heater may help on the coldest nights.

search_results.title: Why your heat pump sometimes blows steam
search_results.snippet: In cold, damp weather frost builds up on the outdoor coil. The unit runs a short defrost cycle, briefly reversing the flow to warm the coil and melt the ice. The cloud of steam you may see outside is normal.

search_results.title: Heat pump or gas boiler?
search_results.snippet: Because a heat pump delivers more heat than the electricity it uses, it can cut heating emissions sharply compared with a gas boiler, especially where the grid uses low-carbon power. Upfront cost is usually higher than a boiler.

search_results.title: Sizing and insulation tips
search_results.snippet: Heat pumps work best with low flow temperatures, so good insulation and larger radiators or underfloor heating help. An installer should do a room-by-room heat loss calculation before choosing a unit size.
